rationale: Close two explanation-shaped frontier items with sourced reasoning instead of leaving them as unexplained suspicions. Both the pre-vote round and the transfer TimeoutNow can at most start a real election; becoming leader still requires a majority of the latest configuration's genuine votes under the membership, prior-vote and log-up-to-dateness checks, so the recorded unknowns are narrowed to the liveness-shaped residual that remains.

feedback.answered: Two propositions. First, a pre-vote that treats an unsupported peer as granting cannot substitute for a real vote: the round changes no state or term and winning it only starts a real election, which requires a genuine majority under the same membership, prior-vote and log-up-to-dateness checks. Second, a TimeoutNow that is not validated against the sender or the current term can only start a candidacy, because the resulting campaign still has to win a majority of the latest configuration's real votes.
remaining: Whether an inflated pre-vote tally in a mixed-version cluster causes avoidable election churn (a liveness cost) is not established.
Whether a non-leader or stale peer can use TimeoutNow to cause repeated election rounds is not established.
Whether a committed configuration with no supporting entry survives a restart and is re-derived from the log (b-config-change).

Whether the election restriction always keeps truncation above every committed configuration index, and whether the (setState, setCurrentTerm) pair can be observed as a term regression under an off-thread heartbeat (b-fsm-apply, b-follower-append).
The shutdown branch of processHeartbeat returns without answering the RPC, which a transport consumer waiting for a response would observe.

Whether any caller outside this repository depends on the configuration index reported by GetConfiguration (b-config-readout), and whether the majority-intersection reasoning covers every permitted one-at-a-time change sequence (b-commit-quorum).
feedback.rationale: Both items were explanation-shaped: the reading shows the protective mechanism is the real vote rather than the advisory round, so the map now states that conditional relationship and keeps only the liveness residuals. No candidate premise is affected, and the last audit unit stays available for a further executable question instead of being spent on these liveness residuals.

b-prevote.rationale: Replace the suspicion that a granted-when-unsupported pre-vote could let a partitioned candidate believe it would win: neither the request handler nor the requester changes state or term, and a won pre-vote only starts a real election that is still decided by real votes with the same membership, prior-vote and log-up-to-dateness checks. The residual is the mixed-version case, where counting an unsupported peer as granting can inflate the tally and cause avoidable election churn rather than a wrong leader.
b-prevote.preserves: b-prevote keeps its owner, trigger, no-state-change guard and its consume edge to f-config-membership; the three confirmed findings and every saved candidate rest on the real vote and configuration paths, which are unchanged by this wording.

b-leadership-transfer.rationale: Replace the open question about TimeoutNow validation with its sourced consequence: the handler forwards the receiver into a candidacy and marks it as transfer-originated without consulting the request's term or sender, but the campaign still needs a majority of the latest configuration's real votes, so the effect is an election round rather than a change to quorum or to who may become leader. The residual is the possible repeated election rounds a non-leader or stale peer can trigger.
